==Characteristics==
==={{OoT|-}}===
{{Descriptions OoT}}
[[File:OoT Barinade Introduction.jpg|thumb|left|200px|{{Game Label|{{OoT|-}}}}Barinade's introduction]]
Barinade is a gigantic, parasitic anemone that has taken host [[Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly]]'s digestive system.<ref name="E 149"/> As a result of Barinade's parasitism toward [[Lord Jabu-Jabu]], the Guardian Deity of the Zora has taken to swallowing almost anything that appears on his altar, including [[Princess Ruto]].<ref name="E 149"/>

[[File:OoT Link Fighting Barinade.jpg|thumb|right|320px|{{Game Label|{{OoT|-}}}}Link throwing his Boomerang at Barinade's exposed body]]
In battle, Barinade covers itself with [[Bari]],<ref name="E 165"/> which it appears to have a symbiotic relationship with. These Bari protect its soft body from attack as it fires volleys of [[Electricity]] at [[Link]] from the center of the [[Boss Arena (Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly)|Boss Arena]]. However, Barinade roots itself to the ceiling of Lord Jabu-Jabu's intestines with three tendrils that can be cut by way of Link's [[Boomerang]]. These tendrils share the blue, green, and red colors of the [[Parasitic Tentacle]]s found Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly.{{Note|In all versions of {{OoT}} prior to {{OoT3D}}, these tendrils are simply colored red.}}

When these tendrils are severed, Barinade focuses its tentacles above itself, generating arcs of Electricity that propel five Bari surrounding it outward in a circular fashion. This attack will end after a short period, causing the Bari to float around the Boss Arena as the Electric tentacles refocus and attack Link once more. During this phase, Barinade will alternate between spinning the Bari around the room and attacking directly.

Link can either attack the Bari with the Boomerang or [[Deku Nut]]s to destroy them while they are floating around the room, or attack Barinade's exposed body with the Boomerang, stunning it and leaving both it and the Bari open to attack. Unlike normal Bari, these Bari do not split into [[Biri]] when defeated. After Link does either of these methods of attack, Barinade will rise and command the remaining five Bari protecting its body to spin in a tight circle around it. At this point, Barinade moves around the room, attempting to strike Link with the Bari shield. As before, there are two cycles to this phase. The first occurs as Barinade emits Electricity through its tentacles above it into the surrounding Bari, creating an impenetrable shield. After a short period of time, Barinade stops channeling Electricity this way and focuses its tentacles on Link. At this point, the Bari are susceptible to attack with the Boomerang or Deku Nuts once more, allowing Link to destroy them and create windows to stun Barinade's body with the Boomerang.

When all ten of the Bari protecting Barinade have been destroyed, Barinade begins to spin around the room while electrifying its vulnerable body and firing arcs of Electricity at Link. Link must use the Boomerang to stun Barinade as it is spinning, causing it to fall to the floor. While in this state, it continues to shoot Electricity at Link from its tentacles, but sits open to attacks. Upon sustaining enough damage, Barinade burrows its body into the floor to recover as its tentacles attack Link. For a short period of time, Barinade is invulnerable, forcing Link to dodge the Electricity as Barinade recovers and repeats this phase of spinning about the room.

Upon sustaining enough damage during this phase, Barinade will suddenly grow fleshy welts along its body before exploding. At the site of its death, Barinade leaves behind a [[Heart Container]]. A blue [[Warp Point]] also appears nearby, where Princess Ruto can be found waiting impatiently for Link.<ref name="OoT Princess Ruto"/>

In {{OoT3D}}, after Link completes the [[Forest Temple (Ocarina of Time)|Forest Temple]] and awakens [[Saria]] as the [[Sage of the Forest]], Barinade can be fought again via the [[Boss Challenge]] mode. By returning to his [[Bed]] in [[Link's House]], Link can choose to fight Barinade.<ref name="OoT Sheik"/><ref name="OoT N/A"/> Barinade can be fought individually or, provided Link has awakened both the [[Sage of Shadow|Sages of Shadow]] and [[Sage of Spirit|Spirit]] and cleared all the Boss Challenges at least once, as part of a Gauntlet. In this Gauntlet, Barinade is fought third in a sequence of eight [[Boss]]es. When Barinade is defeated in the Gaunlet, Link is given the choice to open a small [[Treasure Chest]] for a chance to receive an [[Empty Bottle]] or a Heart Container, or a large Treasure Chest for a chance to receive Deku Nuts, an Empty Bottle, or a single [[Recovery Heart]]. These [[Item]]s will be carried into the subsequent battles in the Gauntlet, but cannot be taken out of Link's dream nor used in different Gauntlet attempts.

==Other Appearances==
==={{OoT|-}} (Himekawa)===
{{Noncanon|Start}}
In Chapter 5, "[[Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly (Chapter)|Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly]]", [[Link]] encounters Barinade while exploring [[Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly]]. There, he spots [[Princess Ruto]] being attacked and rushes in to save her from a [[Bari]].<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Link"/> Princess Ruto explains to Link that she cannot leave until she retrieves the [[Spiritual Stone of Water]], pointing at Barinade.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Princess Ruto"/> However, Barinade quickly grabs her with one of its tentacles.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Princess Ruto 2"/> Link throws his [[Boomerang]] toward Barinade, cutting Princess Ruto free from the tentacle while also hitting the Spiritual Stone loose.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Link 2"/><ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Link 3"/> With Princess Ruto free, Link performs a [[Jump Attack]] on Barinade, causing it to explode.<ref name="OoT (Himekawa) Link 4"/>
{{Noncanon|End}}

==Nomenclature==
Barinade's name is a portmanteau of "[[Bari]]", the jellyfish-like [[Monster]]s that Barinade has a connection with, and {{Romanize|トルネード|torunēdo|tornado|2}}, describing its wild, spinning motions.
{{Nomenclature}}
